name: Trusted Relationship

evidence.rationale: Using multi-factor authentication for administrative accounts reduces the success of adversaries breaching trusted third party relationships to compromise those networks and gain access to intended victims.

Implement role-based access control (RBAC) to manage accounts and permissions used by parties in trusted relationships to minimize potential abuse by the party or if the party is compromised by an adversary.

Adversaries abuse connectivity granted to trusted third parties or external organizations to reach enterprise resources. Segmented third-party access restricts those connections to explicitly authorized services and network zones, directly preventing movement beyond the intended trust boundary.
Remove accounts and permissions used by parties in trusted relationships to minimize potential abuse by the party and if the party is compromised by an adversary.

Separating production and non-production environments prevents a trusted integration or relationship available in a less-restricted non-production environment from automatically providing equivalent network reachability into production.

limits: A claim shows that a control can mitigate a technique. It does not show that an implementation is effective.
'none' or 'no_row' means the mapping has no mitigating control. It does not mean that no defence exists.
Claims use ATT&CK Enterprise 16.1, the version that the source mapping uses. See later_version for changes in newer versions.
CIS claims (cis_claims and cis/safeguards) use ATT&CK Enterprise 19.1, the version that the CIS mapping uses.

ATLAS results describe the ATLAS release in versions.atlas, pinned by commit and digest. ATLAS changes often: a later release can add techniques and mitigations. An empty mitigation list means that this release links no mitigation, not that no mitigation exists. agent_related is derived by this project from names.
